items.text: Note; Refer to a/c flight manual for correct empty weight
Type: Hartzell, Constant speed, full feathering.
(a) Drain Fuel — Tank quick drain under each wing just outboard of undercarriage wells
Drain Fuel — Sump drain under each wing at root
(b) Note location of: Axe - beneath LH front seat
Note location of: Fire Extinguisher - beneath RH front seat
Note location of: First Aid Kit - At rear of cabin
Note location of: Fuel Dipstick - front glovebox
Note location of: Fuel Bottle - front glovebox
Note location of: Control lock - pocket behind pilots seat
2. START—UP: Refer Check List Part A
3. RUN—UP: Refer Check List Part B
4. PRE—TAKE OFF: Refer Check List Part C
(a) Normal: Line up and advance throttles smoothly together to full power
Normal: Once a positive rate of climb is established and a landing on the remaining runway is no longer possible, apply brakes and select undercarriage up
Normal: Allow aircraft to accelerate to 100 kts and maintain. Trim if required
(b) Maximum Performance: Line up and apply toe brakes
Maximum Performance: Advance throttles evenly together to full power
Maximum Performance: Lift nose wheel as soon as possible and rotate at approximately 61 knots
Maximum Performance: Retract undercarriage as soon as positive rate of climb is established
Maximum Performance: Accelerate to and maintain 85 knots until all obstacles are cleared
6. CRUISE: Set power as required (refer Section One Part 3). Lean using EGTs
Short field approach at 82 knots with 30° flap
ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKE OFF ROLL:
If collision unavoidable magnetos off, fuel off, master off
2. ENGINE FAILURE AFTER TAKE OFF PRIOR TO ACHIEVING 85 KNOTS:
Maintain at least 75 knots, select full flap
Turn only to avoid major obstacles
If possible magnetos off, fuel off, master off
Ensure airspeed at least 85 knots - Adjust as required
FULL POWER — Mixtures, Pitch Controls and Throttles ALL FULL FORWARD
IDENTIFY DEAD ENGINE - Dead leg, Dead Engine
VERIFY — CLOSE throttle on suspected dead engine
FEATHER DEAD ENGINE — Move Pitch Control fully back
SECURE DEAD ENGINE - Fuel off, Fuel Pump Off, Ignition Off, Alternator Off
MIXTURE LEAN — remain in VMC circle and land

In certain conditions of temperature and density altitude the aircraft's single engine performance can be very marginal. The decision to continue must take these factors into account as well as obstacles in the takeoff area, weather and pilots ability. In any case control of the aircraft is the foremost consideration and if any doubt exists the pilot would be best advised to close both throttles and land straight ahead rather than to risk losing control of the aircraft.
4. ENGINE FAILURE IN CRUISE OR DESCENT:
As above but prior to securing dead engine — Trouble checks — Refer Check List Section 2, Part A. If unsuccessful:
Secure Engine - Refer Check list, Section 2 part B
Safeguard Live Engine - Cowl Flap Open
Safeguard Live Engine - Reduce Power if possible
Safeguard Live Engine - Check fuel state - Crossfeed if necessary (Refer Check List)
Safeguard Live Engine - Monitor temps / pressure
Proceed to nearest suitable airfield and land
Be prepared to land immediately if fire persists
Continue cranking starter to attempt to pull flame into manifold
IF FIRE PERSISTS — Evacuate aircraft, Use fire extinguisher if possible

sections.title: SECTION 2 — EMERGENCY PROCEDURES — PART E — WING OR ENGINE FIRE IN FLIGHT

items.text: Shut off the affected wing or engine fuel selector and boost pump
Secure the affected engine (Use securing inoperative engine checklist)
Turn the navigation and strobe lights off
Set the power & cowl flaps of the operating engine as required
Move the cabin heat control of the affected engine to the cool position
Reduce the electrical load as required and land as soon as practical

sections.title: SECTION 2 — EMERGENCY PROCEDURES — PART F — CABIN FIRE

items.text: At the first sign of smoke, turn the master and alternator switches off
Move the cabin air controls to cool and close all air vents
Locate the source of smoke or fire and if necessary, use the fire extinguisher in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions
Open ventilators after discharging the Extinguisher within the cabin
Land the aeroplane as soon as possible to inspect for damage

sections.title: SECTION 2 — EMERGENCY PROCEDURES — PART G — ENGINE INDUCTION FIRE WHILE STARTING

items.text: In the event of an induction fire, pull the mixture control to the idle cutoff while continuing to crank the engine. Turn both fuel selectors off
If the fire is not extinguished, turn the master, alternator, and magneto switches off
Take the fire extinguisher from its mounting and evacuate the aeroplane. Take appropriate measures to extinguish the fire
